Below is a short description of what’s happening and a single *SEARCH/REPLACE* edit to stop the empty `/**/` from being picked up as a doc‐comment (and entering the markdown sub-highlighter) so that the rest of your code will continue to be highlighted correctly.

1) Bug scenario & root cause  
   - In Dart mode we have a special “doc comment” rule that looks for anything beginning with `/**` and ending with `*/` and then runs a sub-language (markdown) inside it.  
   - That rule is currently written as:
     ```js
     hljs.COMMENT(
       '/\\*\\*',
       '\\*/', { subLanguage: 'markdown', relevance: 0 }
     )
     ```
   - Because it matches *any* `/** ... */`, an empty comment `/**/` is also consumed by the markdown sub-highlighter.  Since there’s no content, the engine never properly exits back to the Dart state, and *all* of the following code is left un-highlighted.

2) Fix  
   - We want to continue to highlight “proper” doc comments (`/** … */`) in markdown, but we must *not* match an empty `/**/`.  
   - The simplest way is to turn the string‐based begin pattern into a regular expression that only matches `/**` when it is *not* immediately followed by a slash (i.e. block comments with some content).  
   - In practice we change the first two arguments of `hljs.COMMENT` from `'/\\*\\*'` / `'\\*/'` to `/\/\*\*(?!\/)/` / `/\*\//`.

Here’s the patch. Note the negative lookahead `(?!\/)` in the begin regex:

```javascript
### src/languages/dart.js
<<<<<<< SEARCH
      hljs.COMMENT(
        '/\\*\\*',
        '\\*/', {
          subLanguage: 'markdown',
          relevance: 0
        }
      ),
=======
      hljs.COMMENT(
        /\/\*\*(?!\/)/,
        /\*\//, {
          subLanguage: 'markdown',
          relevance: 0
        }
      ),
>>>>>>> REPLACE
```

With this change, an *empty* `/**/` will fall through to the normal C-block-comment rule (which doesn’t invoke markdown), and the rest of your Dart code will continue to be highlighted.
